answer: An agent marketplace can weight votes by locked copper-denominated stake rather than by the number of accounts. An attacker who creates a forest of timber-themed identities gains no extra influence unless they lock more capital; splitting the same stake changes nothing. If a vote requires 51% of the stake, the attacker must acquire and immobilize more than half, bearing financing costs and the risk that their position loses value. A crystal-clear audit trail makes each account's stake visible.
